programs.nl_rule:
The input is a 3-row by 9-column grid divided into three 3×3 sections (left, middle, right). Each section contains a distinct pattern made of grey (X) pixels on a black (.) background. The five possible patterns are: (1) a full border frame with an empty center (8 grey cells: all cells except the center), (2) a single grey cell in the center position only, (3) a full top row of three grey cells with the rest black, (4) a full bottom row of three grey cells with the rest black, and (5) an anti-diagonal line of three grey cells running from top-right to bottom-left.

Divide the input grid into three 3×3 sections (columns 0-2, 3-5, 6-8). For each section, identify which of the five grey-pixel patterns it contains, then replace the entire 3×3 section with a solid block of the corresponding color: full border frame (8 cells) → green (G), single center cell (1 cell) → yellow (Y), top row filled (3 cells across the top) → magenta (M), bottom row filled (3 cells across the bottom) → blue (B), anti-diagonal (top-right, center, bottom-left) → maroon (W). The output grid has the same 3×9 dimensions with each 3×3 section uniformly filled with its mapped color.

Both input and output grids are 3 rows by 9 columns. The grid is logically partitioned into three equally sized 3×3 blocks arranged horizontally. The input uses only grey (X) and black (.) pixels. The output uses only solid-color 3×3 blocks drawn from the set {green, yellow, magenta, blue, maroon}, with each block's color determined by the shape pattern in the corresponding input block.

content.text:
Let me think about this task. The rule: 3x9 grid divided into three 3x3 sections. Each section contains one of five patterns of 5s (grey). Map to color, fill whole section with that color.

I need to propose about 8 candidate input grids. Each must be one of the five patterns in each of the three sections... Actually the verifier uses pattern_to_color lookup, which requires exact patterns. So each section must exactly match one of the five patterns.

Let me construct candidate inputs. Each section: one of:
- ring: ((5,5,5),(5,0,5),(5,5,5)) -> 3 green
- center dot: ((0,0,0),(0,5,0),(0,0,0)) -> 4 yellow
- anti-diagonal: ((0,0,5),(0,5,0),(5,0,0)) -> 9 maroon
- bottom row: ((0,0,0),(0,0,0),(5,5,5)) -> 1 blue
- top row: ((5,5,5),(0,0,0),(0,0,0)) -> 6 magenta

I'll create varied combinations. The task's instances vary but essentially it's always 3x9 with three sections. Let me make 8 candidates with different pattern orders.

Let me write them as 3x9 grids (concatenating three 3x3 sections).

Candidate 1: sections [ring, center, anti] 
ring: 555,505,555
center: 000,050,000
anti: 005,050,500
Rows:
row0: 5 5 5 | 0 0 0 | 0 0 5
row1: 5 0 5 | 0 5 0 | 0 5 0
row2: 5 5 5 | 0 0 0 | 5 0 0

Candidate 2: [top, bottom, ring]
top: 555,000,000
bottom: 000,000,555
ring: 555,505,555
row0: 555 000 555
row1: 000 000 505
row2: 000 555 555

Candidate 3: [anti, ring, center]
anti: 005,050,500
ring: 555,505,555
center: 000,050,000
row0: 005 555 000
row1: 050 505 050
row2: 500 555 000

Candidate 4: [bottom, top, anti]
bottom: 000,000,555
top: 555,000,000
anti: 005,050,500
row0: 000 555 005
row1: 000 000 050
row2: 555 000 500

Candidate 5: [center, anti, bottom]
center: 000,050,000
anti: 005,050,500
bottom: 000,000,555
row0: 000 005 000
row1: 050 050 000
row2: 000 500 555

Candidate 6: [ring, bottom, top]
ring: 555,505,555
bottom: 000,000,555
top: 555,000,000
row0: 555 000 555
row1: 505 000 000
row2: 555 555 000

Candidate 7: [top, center, anti]
row0: 555 000 005
row1: 000 050 050
row2: 000 000 500

Candidate 8: [anti, bottom, ring]
anti: 005,050,500
bottom: 000,000,555
ring: 555,505,555
row0: 005 000 555
row1: 050 000 505
row2: 500 555 555

These all vary. Good. Let me submit.

Actually the instruction says different sizes within half to double — but the rule fixes 3x9. The verifier requires exact 3x3 patterns, so sizes must be 3x9. I'll keep 3x9.

Let me call propose_inputs.

content.text:
The environment asked 6 inputs, 6 wrong, showed 1, 1 flipped correct after. Hmm, student_calls_left: 0. Let me look: "different background colour" refused 3 - those are grids with 0 background but... wait, actually 3 were set aside. Let me check which. The refusal reason "different background colour" - odd. Actually it may mean sections that aren't grey on black? Hmm.

Wait, "n_out_of_band": 3. Those are inputs not instances. Reasons: different background colour. My grids: all use 5 and 0. Hmm. Maybe some sections need... Actually maybe the issue is grids where sections don't form valid patterns? No, all my sections are valid patterns.

Hmm wait, let me recheck. Actually maybe the "background colour" thing refers to... Hmm. Let me recount. Candidates 1-8. Which are invalid? Let me verify each section is exactly one of the 5 patterns.

Candidate 1: sec1 ring ✓, sec2 center ✓, sec3 anti: rows 005,050,500 ✓. Valid.
Candidate 2: sec1 top 555,000,000 ✓, sec2 bottom 000,000,555 ✓, sec3 ring ✓. Valid.
Candidate 3: sec1 anti ✓, sec2 ring ✓, sec3 center ✓. Valid.
Candidate 4: sec1 bottom ✓, sec2 top ✓, sec3 anti ✓. Valid.
Candidate 5: sec1 center ✓, sec2 anti: 005,050,500 ✓, sec3 bottom ✓. Valid.
Candidate 6: sec1 ring ✓, sec2 bottom ✓, sec3 top ✓. Valid.
Candidate 7: sec1 anti ✓, sec2 center ✓, sec3 top... wait candidate 7 row0: 555 000 005. sec1 = rows: row0 555, row1 000, row2 000 → top ✓. sec2: 000,050,000 center ✓. sec3: 005,050,500 anti ✓. Valid.
Candidate 8: sec1 anti ✓, sec2 bottom ✓, sec3 ring ✓. Valid.

Hmm all valid. So why 3 out of band "different background colour"? Odd. Maybe the verifier's concern is... hmm. Perhaps the student's history. Actually "n_asked": 6 of accepted 5? That's weird — asked 6 but only 5 accepted? Maybe includes the example? Hmm.

Anyway, next step: environment already ran. student_calls_left: 0. So I can't query anymore? "student_calls_left": 0. But I can still show_transformed_input maybe. Hmm.

Actually the note says the environment asked a student 6 of my inputs automatically. It showed 1 as demonstration, and 1 other flipped correct. n_still_wrong: 4.

"student_calls_left": 0 — meaning I have no more query calls? Then I should just show demonstrations with show_transformed_input to teach, then start_exam.

Let me think: student_calls_left 0. So query_student may be exhausted. I can still use show_transformed_input / show_example.

I should show more demonstrations to teach the remaining patterns. The student got 1 shown. I need to show examples covering all 5 patterns. Let me use show_transformed_input with inputs that exercise the patterns the student likely doesn't know.

Actually, showing pairs teaches. Let me show a set of inputs covering all five patterns clearly.

Let me use show_transformed_input for a few key grids. But wait, will showing teach? The student learns from demonstrations. Let me show inputs covering each pattern once.

Actually the concern: with student_calls_left 0, maybe I should be careful about how many shows. There's no limit mentioned on show calls.

Let me show a few transformed inputs. I'll pick grids that demonstrate each pattern in different positions.

Let me do show_transformed_input with candidate covering all 5 patterns? Only 3 sections per grid. So need multiple grids.

Grid A: [ring, center, anti] - candidate 1.
Grid B: [top, bottom, ring] - candidate 2.
Grid C: [anti, ring, center] etc.

Actually 1 example already. Let me show about 3-4 transformed inputs to cover all 5 patterns.

Hmm, but I worry the environment might again auto-ask. Let me just show transformed inputs.

Let me show candidate 3 and candidate 6 to cover remaining patterns. Actually ring appears; let me cover: top(row), bottom(row), center, anti, ring.

Candidate 1 gives ring, center, anti. Candidate 2 gives top, bottom, ring. Together cover all 5. So show candidate 1 and candidate 2 as transformed inputs.

But candidate 1 might have been shown already? The example shown was one of the 6 asked. Unknown which. Let me just show candidate 1 and candidate 2.

Actually, let's show a few to be safe: candidate 1, 2, 5.

Let me proceed.
